statement_en: Consider $$\sum_n \frac{1}{n} = \sum_n (-1)^n \frac{(-1)^n}{n}.$$ Let $b_n = (-1)^n$, whose partial sums are bounded, and let $a_n = \frac{(-1)^n}{n} \to 0$, but $a_n$ is not monotone. In fact, this series diverges.
callout_body: $$\sum_n \frac{1}{n} = \sum_n (-1)^n \frac{(-1)^n}{n}$$令$b_n = (-1)^n$其和一定是有界的，$a_n = \frac{(-1)^n}{n} \to0$，不过 $a_n$并不单调。事实上这个级数发散。
